# gr-limesdr

**GNU Radio blocks for LimeSDR hardware**

- **Version recorded:** 3.0.1.10.69
- **Categories:** `sdr-hardware`, `sdr-toolkits`
- **Upstream:** <https://wiki.myriadrf.org/Gr-limesdr_Plugin_for_GNURadio>
- **Needs first:** `gnuradio`

## What it does

Native GNU Radio source and sink blocks for the LimeSDR family, exposing the device's own controls -- per-channel gain stages, the analogue and digital filter chain, NCO and calibration -- rather than the lowest common denominator a generic wrapper offers.

## Why you would want it

You can reach a LimeSDR through gr-osmosdr or SoapySDR, and for simple receive that is enough. This is for when it is not: full-duplex operation, both channels at once, and the filter and calibration control that MIMO and transmit work actually need.

## Before it will work

LimeSDR hardware and LimeSuite, which this catalog carries separately. Device firmware and gateware must match the LimeSuite version, and that mismatch is the most common LimeSDR problem.

## Install and launch

- **Installed by name only** — it is in no profile.
- **Install:** `hammunition install gr-limesdr --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Its package ships its own commands and application-menu entry; a unit that ships none gets a generated terminal entry (**D-050**). `hammunition status` lists what is installed.
- **The install needs the network to:** your distribution's package archive.

## Offline use

*Not yet documented for this application.* Read “Before it will work” above for what it needs; the install-time network line above is the only offline fact generated from the manifest. Internet, a local network and a radio link are three different things, and this page does not claim any of them works until it says so.

## Known problems

The maintainer does not own this hardware, so nothing here is maintainer-verified (D-027) -- it is carried because other operators have the devices. Version-locked to GNU Radio like every out-of-tree module. LimeSDR transmits, and what you emit is your responsibility.
